Asturian

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

cambiare

  1. first-person singular pluperfect indicative of cambiar
  2. third-person singular pluperfect indicative of cambiar
  3. first-person singular imperfect subjunctive of cambiar
  4. third-person singular imperfect subjunctive of cambiar

Italian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cambiar (apocopic)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin or Late Latin cambiāre, from change in conjugation of cambīre. Doublet of cangiare. Cognate with Neapolitan cagnà.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kamˈbja.re/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -are
  • Hyphenation: cam‧bià‧re

Verb

[edit]

cambiàre (first-person singular present càmbio, first-person singular past historic cambiài, past participle cambiàto, auxiliary (transitive) avére or (intransitive) èssere)

  1. (transitive) to exchange
    cambiare denaro ― to exchange money
  2. (transitive) to change
    cambiare faccia ― to change face
  3. (intransitive) to change [auxiliary essere]

[edit]

[edit]

cambiāre (Late Latin)

  1. present active infinitive of cambiō (“to exchange, barter”)

Related terms

[edit]

Leonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Leonese [Term?], from Vulgar Latin or Late Latin cambiāre, from change in conjugation of cambīre, of Gaulish origin. Compare Asturian cambiar.

Verb

[edit]

cambiare

  1. to change

References

[edit]
  • “cambiare”, in Diccionario Castellano-Leonés / Leonés-Castellano [Spanish-Leonese / Leonese-Spanish Dictionary] (in Spanish), La Asociación L'Alderique, 2012–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

cambiare

  1. first/third-person singular future subjunctive of cambiar
